label: X-01
evidence: crates/sealmap/src/main.rs:659-682 (fn sign): Ctx::load reads the lock once (L660-662), seal::sign mutates it in memory (L670), then plain fs::write of the topic (L679-680) followed by a separate plain fs::write of seals.lock (L682); no temp-file+rename, file lock, CAS or fsync anywhere in crates/sealmap/src or crates/sealmap-corpus/src (grep for rename/flock/tempfile/atomic finds nothing relevant). lock.rs:27-31 doc only argues git-merge disjointness. check.rs:337-340 documents unparsable lock -> single LockFault. The first report's main.rs:612-634 line numbers are off by about 48 lines, but the code it describes is present.
rationale: Unlocked read-modify-write and non-atomic truncating writes really are there, so concurrent signers can lose entries and a crash can truncate the lock. The consequences are overstated: the gate fails closed, and the risk needs concurrent use in one checkout.

label: X-02
evidence: crates/sealmap-rust/src/resolve.rs:60 has "Self" in PRELUDE, but Resolver::call at resolve.rs:818-829 matches "Self" before the PRELUDE drop arm: it returns None only when ctx.self_ty is None (L824). Otherwise "Self" | "self" falls through (L825) to resolve_in, and walk resolves "Self" to self_ty (L655).
rationale: Self::f() calls inside an impl or trait are explicitly exempt from the prelude drop and resolve against the self type. The claimed join of the two facts does not hold.

README.md:191 and 197-198 make the unqualified rustfmt and reflow claim. docs/diagrams/REGISTER.md:40 (DB-20) and docs/diagrams/extract/06-...md:45-47 acknowledge the gap. .github/workflows has no reflow job.
rationale: The gap is real and visible in code, though narrower than claimed, because trailing commas are normalised at token level and rustfmt leaves most non-expression macros alone. It is a registered known limitation, not a hidden one, and the claimed scale of false findings is unmeasured.

label: X-05
evidence: crates/sealmap-rust/src/lib.rs:154 says 'Never fails'. crates/sealmap-extract/src/isolate.rs:8-10 and 46 show catch_unwind, which cannot catch stack overflow. crates/sealmap-rust/src/collect.rs:30 and 1113 apply MAX_EXPR_DEPTH=1024 only in the flow walker, after syn::parse_file (collect.rs:44). sealmap-model/src/source.rs:65 admits files up to 2 MiB. Reproduced with the release build of sealmap at this revision: a 40 KB lib.rs holding 20,000 nested parentheses, and 'type T = Vec<...>' nested 100,000 deep, both made `sealmap model .` abort with 'has overflowed its stack ... aborting' (exit 134). 10,000 parentheses passed.
rationale: A small admissible input aborts the whole process instead of producing a per-file diagnostic, so the no-fail contract is broken. I did not isolate whether the overflow happens in syn's parser or a later recursive pass, but the core defect is reproduced.
